note: Pinned revisions of the sibling repositories sb3-creator's cross-repo gates consume. CI checks these exact commits out beside the repo (.github/workflows/ci.yml) so the gates RUN rather than skip; test/helpers/siblings.mjs turns an absent sibling into a failure when CI=true. Update a pin deliberately, in its own commit, with the suite green against it. `rev` MUST be the FULL 40-character SHA: actions/checkout only recognises a full SHA as a commit, and turns anything shorter into `git fetch origin +refs/heads/<ref>*` — a branch glob that matches nothing. An abbreviated pin here took every CI run on main down at the checkout step, before lint, tests, the mutation prover or the build ran at all. gate-integrity asserts the length; `revShort` exists only for prose.

bw-board.why: the device/board simulator the gallery e2e and physics gates drive. BUMPED 2026-09-08 from 338ac5d to master's tip 7b7f3b5, and the bump is FORCED by DEVICE REGISTRATION that postdates the previous pin: src/devices/retro-dips.js registers the Intel 8086 CPU and 8255 PPI (registerDevice('i8086', ...) at retro-dips.js:200 and registerDevice('i8255', ...) at :202). At 338ac5d those chips' FILES existed (src/i8255.js, i8086-adapter.js, i8086-extract.js) but the DEVICES were not registered — and that is the distinction that decides the failure. bw-circuit-ui's engineKindFor() keeps a PASSTHROUGH_KINDS kind only if the engine resolves a device model for it (eng.getDevice(kind)); otherwise it collapses to a generic 'mcu'. So the incoming i8086-blink example's cpu86 (kind i8086) loaded as a generic 40-pin MCU, and every address-bus wire named a terminal that generic surface does not declare — 51 example-corpus-contract violations, one cause. Files present is not the same as a kind registered. Measured against 7b7f3b5: cpu86 resolves as i8086 with its 40 declared terminals, Circuit.fromJSON reports no netlistError, and the corpus-contract per-terminal check clears. This range is 426 commits over the SOLVER, so RE-DERIVED rather than re-stamped: expected-quantities-hold re-solves every numeric claim against bw-board@7b7f3b5 + bw-circuit-ui@c276c0d and PASSES with no new mismatches and the recorded exceptions unchanged; the provenance re-stamp is exactly one bw-board@ revision line per page, every per-page census count and every prose quantity byte-identical — the solver produces the same numbers across the range. bw-board master CI is green on 7b7f3b5.
